To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the plasma ANF response during exercise in the heat is blunted compared to exercise in the cold, and that this blunting is due to the increased plasma volume and the associated decreased plasma osmolality.
plasma levels of ANF increase during high intensity submaxial exercise in the heat, but not in the cool.

(a) plasma ANF increased significantly in the heat, but not in the cold, and was correlated with plasma volume; (b) plasma ANF decreased significantly after 30 and 60 minutes of high intensity exercise in the heat, with no significant change after 90 minutes; and (c) plasma ANF did not change significantly after high intensity exercise in both heat and cold.

the human body has a very complex system that is able to maintain homeostasis during exercise and in the heat.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the ANF response to heat stress during high intensity submaximally exercise is blunted.
the human body has a remarkable capacity to respond to heat stress, and the cardiovascular system is one of the most important organs that help to keep us cool.
the body's natural defenses against the harmful effects of exercise in the heat can be overwhelmed by the heat and/or by the exercise itself.
